blockers.title: Bound local backup import and encryption/decryption resources
blockers.reproduction: Previously the local backup reader called File.text(), JSON.parse(), atob(), and crypto.subtle decrypt on files and ciphertext without explicit byte limits; oversized multibyte JSON can use substantially more UTF-8 bytes than JS string length.
blockers.rootCause: Backup import/export/crypto lacked consistent upfront UTF-8 and envelope resource limits, including file metadata preflight and authenticated ciphertext bounds. Subsequent review also found salt/IV were decoded prior to field-level preflight and decrypted bytes used non-fatal UTF-8 decoding.
blockers.fixes: Added deterministic 64 MiB UTF-8 JSON and 96 MiB encrypted-envelope cap, compatible with the existing connected-recovery 100 MiB bound; fail-closed file.size gate before File.text(), JSON.parse gate, encryption gate before key derivation, ciphertext base64 length bound before atob/PBKDF2, and authenticated plaintext byte bound before decoding. No records are truncated or modified when refused. Current continuation adds fixed-size canonical salt/IV and ciphertext-base64 preflight before atob/PBKDF2 and strict UTF-8 decoding after authentication; invalid authenticated bytes fail closed.
blockers.acceptance: Run full client Vitest/types/build, browser and real IndexedDB restore on both valid and oversized files, wrong keys and corrupted envelopes; measure memory/quota on low-end Windows and agree safe supported archive sizes with owner. Large historical archives requiring a higher cap need an approved streamed/import-recovery design, never silent truncation.
